key_insight: AI-based MRI radiomics showed good accuracy for preoperative detection of tumor deposits in rectal cancer, with pooled sensitivity of 76.5% and specificity of 79.0%.
clinical_relevance: Detecting tumor deposits before surgery could inform risk stratification, although these findings do not establish readiness for routine clinical use.
method: Systematic review and bivariate diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis.
Evaluated MRI radiomics against histopathology in adults with rectal cancer.
Compared MRI sequences and radiomics-only versus combined clinical/radiological models.
evidence_signal: Across 9 studies involving 2,589 patients, pooled AUC was 0.845 and validation-dataset AUC was 0.806; combined models had higher sensitivity than radiomics alone (84.2% vs 65.7%, p<0.001).
watch_item: MRI-sequence subgroup differences were not statistically significant, so superiority of T2WI plus DWI remains uncertain.
paper_title: AI-Based MRI Radiomics for Preoperative Detection of Tumor Deposits in Rectal Cancer: A Bivariate Diagnostic Accuracy Meta-analysis
